layers: React/Vite client: UI routes, auth context, ephemeral cart/wishlist, and mock/live API seam.
Express API: validation, endpoint orchestration, JWT middleware, integrations, and static dist serving.
Domain modules: catalogue projection, Zod validation/pricing, auth, Razorpay, and notifications.
Persistence: MySQL and deterministic in-memory fallback; additive SQL migrations and seeding.

main_modules.src/App.jsx: Client routes, storefront/admin pages, shared UI, cart/wishlist state, and live data access.
main_modules.src/mockData.js: Prototype content and deterministic seed inputs.
main_modules.src/context/AuthContext.jsx: User auth state/actions persisted to localStorage.
main_modules.server/index.js: REST declarations, middleware, order/payment/auth coordination, uploads, and SPA fallback.
main_modules.server/repository.js: Memory/MySQL repository implementations and DB failure fallback.
main_modules.server/pricing.js: Zod schemas and server-derived order/payment amounts.
main_modules.server/auth.js: User/admin identity, JWTs, guards, and reset flow.

architecture.request_flow: Browser loads src/main.jsx -> App routes. Vite proxies /api to Express:4000 in development. Express validates/authenticates requests, invokes domain modules and repository, then returns JSON. Production Express serves dist/index.html for non-API routes.
architecture.data_flow: src/mockData.js supplies prototype content and server/catalog.js seed projections. Live requests use API helpers. Orders/custom requests are validated; pricing uses server catalogue/settings before persistence.
architecture.state_management: React state owns cart/wishlist and is ephemeral. AuthContext persists user token/data in localStorage. App-level context shares live data.
architecture.authentication_authorization: User/admin JWTs are issued and checked in server/auth.js; protected endpoints use requireUserJWT/requireAdminJWT and the client has ProtectedRoute. A development fallback JWT secret exists; Google auth handler accepts client identity fields, so do not treat it as verified without trusted token verification.
architecture.database_storage: DATABASE_URL or DB_HOST enables MySQL; otherwise memory mode. Configured MySQL has per-operation in-memory fallback on DB errors; fallback writes are not durable. Run migrations and seed for managed persistence.
architecture.external_services: Optional Razorpay; missing config results in mock payment behavior. Notifications are config-gated and can use Gmail/owner path. No verified Google token exchange was identified.
architecture.background_jobs: No scheduler, queue, or background worker detected. Notifications are triggered during request handling.
architecture.build_deploy_flow: npm run build creates dist. Docker uses Node 22 Alpine, npm ci --omit=dev, builds, then runs npm start. Production API listens on PORT or 3000.

conventions: Frontend follows src/pages, src/context, and src/components, but most storefront/admin implementation is concentrated in src/App.jsx.
Backend uses ESM and named exports; API routes are declared directly in server/index.js.
Async route handlers generally forward errors to Express next(error).
Zod in server/pricing.js validates checkout/custom request payloads; keep pricing authoritative on the server.
Shared mock catalogue also feeds backend seeding; do not treat it as durable order/customer state.
Add numbered SQL migrations under server/migrations; repository behavior should be implemented in both memory and MySQL variants.
No test, lint, formatter, or typecheck scripts/files were found.
Migration runner logs and continues after individual statement errors; inspect schema/logs.
DB fallback is in-memory and per operation; data may be non-durable or split when MySQL returns.
Planning/TODO documents include earlier or aspirational scope; runtime source/scripts are authoritative.
No inheritance or obvious direct circular imports found by static import-path heuristic; dead exports and indirect cycles are not proven.
